purpose: Prevent cross-chat deadlocks caused by checkpoints that record runner hashes without persisting the exact source bytes required for deterministic continuation.

definitions.continuation_critical_source: Any runner, scorer, materializer, finalizer, converter, parity engine, or other executable source whose exact implementation is required to reproduce, rematerialize, validate, or continue an authoritative checkpoint.
definitions.durable_source: Exact source bytes stored in persistent repository authority and verified by independent readback SHA-256.
definitions.hash_only_reference: A filename and/or SHA-256 recorded without recoverable exact source bytes. A hash-only reference is identity evidence but is NOT sufficient resumability evidence.

mandatory_promotion_gate.rule: A checkpoint or HEAD MUST NOT be promoted as cross-chat resumable when any continuation-critical source lacks durable exact source bytes.
mandatory_promotion_gate.pass_condition: For every required_for_continuation=true source, source_sha256 == readback_sha256 AND readback_verified=true AND repository_path resolves to the exact bytes.
mandatory_promotion_gate.fail_condition: Any missing source bytes, missing locator, hash mismatch, or unverified readback fails closed and forbids resumable promotion.

source_storage_policy.normalization: NONE_AFTER_FREEZE; newline or encoding changes create a new source identity

derived_artifact_rule.rule: Absence of a derived runtime artifact alone is not a blocker when canonical inputs, durable exact source bytes, dependency contract, and expected output hash permit exact deterministic rematerialization.

legacy_missing_source_migration.rule: Historical missing source bytes MUST NOT be fabricated, silently reconstructed under the old hash, or treated as recovered.
legacy_missing_source_migration.allowed_route: Create a new implementation with a new immutable source SHA under a preregistered IMPLEMENTATION_MIGRATION bridge.
requirements: Preserve the legacy filename and SHA as SOURCE_BYTES_UNAVAILABLE historical identities.
Freeze the replacement source bytes in GitHub BEFORE evaluating the pending scientific shard.
Use only previously exposed development evidence for equivalence validation; do not access holdout.
Require exact signal identity where applicable and exact ordered trade-ledger parity where recoverable.
Require zero rule changes to signal, execution, risk, cost, and selection semantics.
A failed equivalence test blocks the replacement; it must not be tuned retrospectively to the pending shard's economic result.
Only after the equivalence gate passes may the replacement implementation be used prospectively on work that was not previously promoted.

negative_tests: One-byte source mutation must fail source SHA before execution.
Wrong expected source SHA must fail closed.
Missing repository path must fail closed.
Executed canonical source must emit the exact deterministic stdout SHA.

adoption_condition: CANARY must be recovered and executed from a fresh chat/runtime using GitHub only, with all positive and negative tests passing. Until then this policy is not allowed to modify the scientific HEAD.
